t: The Commonwealth joined Poland and Lithuania in 1569 into one of Europe's largest states, with an elected king and noble parliament.
Its religious tolerance made it a refuge for dissenters and home to the world's largest Jewish population.
The liberum veto paralysed reform, letting Russia, Prussia and Austria partition it out of existence by 1795.
dyk: In 1610, after the victory at Klushino, Polish troops occupied Moscow and a group of boyars elected the Polish prince Władysław as Tsar.
ev: The Union of Lublin creates the Commonwealth from Poland and Lithuania
The Warsaw Confederation guarantees religious peace among the nobility
Żółkiewski wins at Klushino and Polish troops occupy Moscow
Bohdan Khmelnytsky's Cossack uprising begins in Ukraine
Władysław Siciński breaks up the Sejm with a single objection, the first liberum veto
Jan III Sobieski leads the cavalry charge that relieves Vienna
The Constitution of 3 May abolishes the liberum veto
The Third Partition erases the Commonwealth from the map

f.predecessor: Kingdom of Poland, Grand Duchy of Lithuania
